note: Rounds 1 and 2 of the owner's 2026-11-21 directive: TestSprite as the independent layer. Each run reached this machine through a tunnel (testsprite test run <id> --local 3000) against the production bundle on :3000 with a real PostgreSQL behind it. Plans are generated by qa/testsprite/plans.mjs from the live fixture, and a created test carries that tenant's id for ever -- so re-running the fixture means regenerating and creating again.

runs.journey: Signing in reaches the Command Center, not a session diagnostic
The revenue report separates collected from invoiced
A withheld field on a member's record is marked, never blank
runs.finding: The first run of this journey failed, and the defect was real. The plan asserted the member's own name was readable; it is not, because an identity field needs a stepped-up session and a name is one. What the tester did next is the finding: it clicked the withheld marker looking for a way through, and on /members there was none -- the step-up that lifts the mask was offered on a member's record only. The offer is on the list now, pointing back at the list, and tests/e2e/members.spec.ts asserts it.

runs.journey: A report a front-desk session cannot open is absent, not locked
runs.note: The corrected plan: it signs in as the front desk, which holds the person read and nothing of the money modules, which is the session the canvas's sentence is about.

runs.journey: The owner, who holds everything, is listed both reports
runs.note: The other half of the gate, which the original plan conflated with the first.

runs.journey: A booking inside a coach's time off is shown and flagged, not quietly dropped
runs.found: ADM-SCH-04, and it failed twice before it passed. The first run: 'The week grid shows all 112 hours as available and unbooked' -- the page opened on the current week and had no way to leave it, so the exception, which is agreed ahead of the day it covers and is the canvas's own example, was unreachable from the screen. `here({ from })` existed in the page and nothing called it. Every in-repo spec navigates straight to `?from=`, so none of them could notice. The second run, with the navigation built, failed for a different and legitimate reason: the plan did not say a person would move between weeks to find a day off. The third passed.

correction: The journey 'A report this session cannot open is absent, not locked' failed three times against a product that was right, and the fault was the plan. Its description quoted the canvas's Club Manager scenario -- 'the two financial ones are absent' -- while its steps signed in as the owner, so the agent checked the financial reports were absent for a session holding every permission and reported them present. It was right to. A plan's description is read as the specification, which is the point of writing them in English; one that describes a different session from the one the steps open is a plan contradicting itself. It is now the two halves it should always have been. The misdiagnosis in between is written up in contracts/ui/design-compliance.md: a theory that explains a failure is not the cause of it.
